messages:
harper: Quick note from staging: SLO cards show 'Alerts: 7' for tenant X even though quiet-mode and quota should have suppressed notifications. Owners are confused.
samir: I can reproduce. Quiet-mode stops fanout but our SLO summary API still reports raw event counts. UI was using that for the burn widget.
toni: That's an API contract problem. Consumers expect the burn number to reflect outgoing notifications, not raw signals.
harper: Proposed change: have the API return both `raw_signals` and `outgoing_burn` (server applies quiet/quota/routing logic to compute outgoing estimate). Console displays `outgoing_burn` by default and shows `raw_signals` as secondary.
samir: Implementation: compute `suppressed_by_quiet` and `dropped_by_quota` during aggregation window and set `outgoing_burn = raw_signals - suppressed_by_quiet - dropped_by_quota`. Ship behind a feature flag.
toni: Frontend: prefer `outgoing_burn` when present. Also show a tiny pill when quiet is active: "Quiet until <ts> notifications paused". Keep raw signals under a chevron for advanced view.
harper: Caching note: console caches /slo/summary for 30s. For tenant-scoped views reduce TTL to 5s while canary is active to avoid stale spikes.
samir: Telemetry: emit `slo.signals.raw`, `slo.signals.outgoing`, and `slo.signals.delta` (raw - outgoing). Add an alert if delta > 20 for > 5 minutes during rollout.
toni: Tests: overlapping quiet windows, simultaneous quota and quiet, and late-arriving events. Add end-to-end smoke asserting UI uses outgoing_burn when server provides it.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled for staging 2026-04-12T08:00Z tag=outgoing-burn-canary. Rollout steps: server FF -> console reads outgoing_burn if present -> reduce TTL -> smoke -> monitor telemetry -> promote.
harper: I'll open the RFC and server PR. Toni can you own the UI changes and copy? Samir take telemetry and alert rule?
samir: Yep. I'll draft the alert and Grafana comparators.
toni: Sync 20m tomorrow 10:30 PT. Thanks.
